fields.mutation_checks: run on the exact source tree before it was committed, with private tooling that applies one exact replacement, runs the engine's filtered library tests and restores the file; the three specifications and their results are attached to the batch23-source stage. First run: 14 single mutations over the F2 rule, the F3 binding and budget checks, the receipt's canonical representation in completion, the coordinator's artifact creation event, completion's transaction-receipt comparison and the start-time flush; 11 made their expected test fail. The three survivors were resolved before the commit: the forged receipt case was made self-consistent with its snapshot, so only the canonical representation can refuse it; the stale receipt is refused by three independent bindings (the call, the action and the result digest), so removing one clause cannot make it pass; and the real budget owner does not depend on the coordinator's flush, which only the synthetic test pins. The composed test also found the owner defect fixed in this batch. A rerun of 13 (the two reworked mutations and eleven over the owner's new terminal check) caught 8; the five clauses the journal already enforces (sequence, predecessor, run, session and task) survived because the store refused those terminals with an integrity failure, so they were removed from the check. A final run of the six remaining owner-check mutations caught all six
